recipes.name: Pesto Chicken
ingredients_raw: 4 thin slices prosciutto, or more if needed

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease a baking dish.

Spread about 2 tablespoons of pesto per chicken breast over the top of each breast, and wrap each breast in prosciutto slices to cover the entire breast. Place the wrapped chicken breasts into the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until the chicken is no longer pink, the juices run clear, and the prosciutto is lightly crisped, about 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pesto Chicken
raw_recipe.description: So simple. Spread skinless, boneless chicken breasts with basil pesto, wrap in prosciutto, and bake for an Italian-inspired main dish that's ready in only 35 minutes. Eat it hot with pasta, or let cool and slice for a salad.

video.description: This easy chicken combines pesto and prosciutto for a quick and delicious dinner!

review.reviewBody: This recipe was fantastic! So easy too. I marinated chicken for a few hours in a citrus, onion, mustard seed marinade and used bacon instead of prosciutto. I'm no chef but this recipe sure made me seem like one. Delicious. Thanks for posting.

Made it last week, was delicious! I cut the chicken breasts lengthwise and added pesto sauce and mozzarella cheese, then rolled the pieces up. Once the chicken was cooked and the bacon is crisp, added more mozzarella cheese, it was delicious!
Pound chicken and Marinated ahead of time . I used bacon to wrap then used a rack to lift chicken in pan because bacon made fat drippings.

This was by far the easiest, most delicious meal I think I've ever cooked. I bought prego basil pesto smeared it all over the chicken and wrapped bacon around it. Threw it in the oven for 30 minutes and oh my gosh the tenderness and amount of flavor was amazing. It took 3 minutes to prepare and looked like something out of a magazine. Super easy, but looks like you put major effort into it. Will most certainly be making this many more times!

I butterflied the breasts. Seasoned with s &p, no salt seasoning and garlic powder. Mixed in 2 tblsp of artichoke and Asiago dip with the pesto. No need to use toothpicks. Then wrapped in prosciutto . Lots of juice and oil to baste with. Next time use less salt or no salt. The prosciutto provides it. Serve with roast baby potatoes and steamed veggies or a side salad. Will make again.
Made with homemade vegan pesto, delicious! Baked for 15 mins covered, 15 mins uncovered. Very moist.
I used bacon instead of pruscuitto. I also added crumbled feta. Baked it at 400 for 25 minutes then broiled it for about 3 minutes to make the bacon crispy! Served with rice and broccoli!

I liked it. I used the advice of another reviewer and put the ham on the inside of the rolled chicken. I also included some sautéed mushrooms. I brushed the chicken with egg and sprinkled with bread crumbs to ensure it browned. I served it with pasta also tossed in pesto - it was quite good.

Delicious! So much easier than stuffing the breast. Didn’t have quite enough Pesto so I mixed with Neufchâtel cheese to make enough. It was still flavorful enough. We had different sized breasts so we cut the small in half and the large in thirds so they were all the same size. Served on top of a bed of fettuccine tossed with a little leftover garlic butter I had frozen and some parsley flakes.

Been on a diet and always looking for ways to cut back carbs. So simple to make! I pounded the chicken flat. I used thick cut applewood smoked bacon and Canadian bacon with fresh garlic. Chicken, Pesto, Garlic, Canadian Bacon then smoked bacon and rolled it up. I baked it at 350 for 40 min to make sure the thick cut bacon cooked through. Served it with a seasoned Cauliflower mash and it was great! No to low carb and I will be making this one again.
This was delicious!!! I added mozzarella to the pesto mix and topped it with homemade creamy pesto sauce. I will definitely make this again.

Ok so I really wanted to stick to the recipe I spite of the fact that I really felt that the chicken breast was too thick as it was and the prosciutto will dry. But then I cooked pretty much all the things you can wrap in bacon wrapped in bacon so wanted to try something different. And I learned some things. The first one is that the real prosciutto do Parma is harder to work with and you need more than two slices and before you know it the prosciutto will cost you more than the chicken. The less fancy prosciutto was a bit thicker and it worked much better. And the third thing was that the prosciutto actually held up pretty well in terms of being moist enough by the time the chicken was done. Next time I will probably cut the chicken breast in two smaller pieces lengthwise. Or use chicken tenders.
Made it exactly to directions and we loved it. Sliced up one leftover breast and used it in a salad the next day. Also yummy!
I added some parsley flakes, black garlic, and onion salt to the top of the chicken. One of the greatest hits in our home.

This was great, and so easy! I love how moist the chicken breast turns out with the pesto filling and prosciutto wrap. I did mine with 6 larger chicken tenders, because that’s what I had, and it worked well.
Family thought it was good. Will make again, very easy and fancy looking. Went great with an herbed rice.
Thin procuitto was tasty but a bit dried out. I might prefer with a thicker slice r perhaps cook part of the time covered.
Very disappointed after all the good reviews. Recipe definitely needs tweaking.
This was good! The very last 5 minutes I added a slice of Muenster cheese.
